sections.heading: Eclipse Information, Accuracy and Safety
content: Eclipse paths, times, and other information in the App are provided for general information and exploration. They are predictions based on published catalogue data and calculations, and may be incomplete, approximate, or out of date.
<ul class="list-disc list-outside mb-4 space-y-1 pl-5">

• Not navigation or safety advice. The App is not a navigation, travel, weather, or safety tool. Do not rely on it as your sole source when planning travel, choosing a viewing location, or making any decision where inaccuracy could cause harm or loss.

• Protect your eyes. Looking directly at the Sun, including during a partial eclipse, without suitable eye protection can cause serious and permanent eye damage. Use solar viewing equipment that meets the relevant safety standard (for example, ISO 12312-2) and follow guidance from reputable sources such as national space agencies or eye-health bodies. The App does not provide eye-safety advice and is not a substitute for it.

• Verify independently. Check times, locations, and local conditions with official or specialist sources before you travel or make plans. Weather, terrain, access rules, and local regulations may affect your viewing.
• "Near me". Results relating to your location depend on the accuracy of your device's location services and of the underlying data.
• No guarantee of visibility. We do not guarantee that any eclipse will be visible from any place or at any time.

content: Eclipse predictions in the App are based on catalogue data by Fred Espenak and Jean Meeus, published via NASA. The data is included in the App. Full attribution is shown on the Data Sources screen in the App.
You can learn more from NASA's eclipse resources at eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov.

NASA, Fred Espenak, and Jean Meeus have not reviewed, approved, or endorsed the App, and we do not claim any official status or affiliation. We may process, format, and present this data for use in the App, and that presentation may introduce errors. The authoritative sources remain the original published catalogues.
